title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to obtain families with constant encoding rate and linear distance. We resolve the coupled logical constraints using explicit representatives to characterize the full gauged code space. We provide a fundamental treatment of code distance based on the general Knill--Laflamme condition and combine expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary low-weight errors. We further construct an almost-good family whose entire code space exhibits long-range magic. Gauging and ungauging also enable logical Clifford measurements that prepare encoded magic states. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting and provide a concrete foundation for exploring non-Abelian phases beyond geometric locality and pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture.

bite.hook: New non-Abelian quantum LDPC codes achieve linear distance, constant rate, and long-range magic without 2D limits.
tldr: Constructed non-Abelian quantum LDPC error-correcting codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products.
Proved code distance via the general Knill-Laflamme condition, achieving linear distance and constant encoding rate.
Built an almost-good code family whose entire code space exhibits long-range computational magic.
bite.whyItMatters: Fault-tolerant quantum computing needs low-overhead error correction with universal gates; extending good LDPC codes beyond standard Pauli stabilizers unlocks brand-new topological phases and built-in computational power.
bite.eli5: Traditional quantum error codes are like flat grids of checkerboards that struggle to do complex computations without messy workarounds. This paper weaves higher-dimensional mathematical shapes that not only protect data efficiently, but also have universal computing power baked right in.

glossary.shortDef: Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check code: an error-correcting code where each check acts on few qubits.
glossary.eli5Def: A quantum protection system where error-checking sensors only have to watch a few neighboring bits at a time.

glossary.shortDef: Necessary and sufficient algebraic criteria for a quantum code to protect against a set of errors.
glossary.eli5Def: The mathematical rulebook that proves whether a quantum code can successfully shield data from noise.

glossary.shortDef: A non-stabilizer quantum state required to achieve universal quantum computation via gate teleportation.
glossary.eli5Def: A special, hard-to-make quantum resource that turns a basic quantum calculator into a universal computer.

glossary.shortDef: Operations or symmetries whose order of execution matters (A*B ≠ B*A).
glossary.eli5Def: Actions where the sequence counts—like putting on socks before shoes versus shoes before socks.
